#!/usr/bin/env node
import { greeting } from '../src/greet.js';

const name = process.argv.slice(2).find((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
if (!name) {
  process.stderr.write('usage: greet <name>\n');
  process.exit(2);
}
process.stdout.write(`${greeting(name)}\n`);
{
  "name": "greet-cli",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Greets people",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "index.js",
  "scripts": {
    "test": "node --test"
  },
  "license": "MIT"
}

node bin/greet.js <name>

result.builder:
Goal: one pull request adding a --shout flag to greet-cli that meets these acceptance lines:
1. "node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case"
2. "without --shout the output is unchanged"
3. "docs/index.md documents --shout"
4. "after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout"

Steps:
1. Read bin/greet.js, src/greet.js, test/greet.test.js, docs/index.md and .github/workflows/pages.yml. Today bin/greet.js takes the first argument not starting with `--` as the name and prints `greeting(name)` (`Hello, <name>!`) plus a newline.
2. In bin/greet.js, detect `--shout` anywhere in process.argv.slice(2). When present, print the whole greeting line upper-cased (e.g. `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!\n`); the flag must work whether it comes before or after the name. When absent, the output must stay byte-for-byte what it is now (`Hello, Ada!\n`), and the usage message / exit code 2 for a missing name stays as is. Keep src/greet.js's `greeting` behaviour unchanged (you may add a separate helper if you like).
3. Add tests to test/greet.test.js: `--shout Ada` gives `HELLO, ADA!\n`; `Ada --shout` gives the same; plain `Ada` still gives `Hello, Ada!\n`. Keep the existing tests. Run `npm test` and make sure all pass.
4. Update docs/index.md to document the `--shout` flag: show the usage `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>` and say it prints the greeting in upper case (e.g. `HELLO, <NAME>!`). The literal text `--shout` must appear in the file. Optionally mirror this in README.md.
5. Line 4 is met by publishing: .github/workflows/pages.yml deploys the docs/ directory to GitHub Pages on push to main, so the docs/index.md change is what will appear on https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ once merged. Do not change the workflow, do not try to publish or deploy anything yourself, and do not create a separate docs site. In the PR description, state plainly that line 4 can only be confirmed after merge, once the pages workflow has run.
6. Open one pull request with these changes, listing each acceptance line and how it is met.
result.verifier: Check the pull request at its head commit. Run commands from a checkout of the PR head; run `npm test` first and note the result. One check per acceptance line, in order: Check 1 — "node bin/greet.js --shout prints the greeting in upper case" Run: `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and `node bin/greet.js --shout 'Grace Hopper'`. PASS: each exits 0 and prints the normal greeting for that name in upper case, i.e. `HELLO, ADA!` and `HELLO, GRACE HOPPER!` (each followed by a newline). FAIL: either command errors, exits non-zero, prints lower/mixed case letters, or prints something other than the upper-cased greeting. Check 2 — "without --shout the output is unchanged" Run at the PR head and at the PR's base commit (e.g. `git worktree add` of the merge-base or base, read-only): `node bin/greet.js Ada`, `node bin/greet.js 'Grace Hopper'`, and `node bin/greet.js` (no name; capture stdout, stderr and exit code). PASS: for every command, stdout, stderr and exit code at the PR head are identical to those at the base (expected `Hello, Ada!\n`, `Hello, Grace Hopper!\n`, and the usage message on stderr with exit code 2). FAIL: any difference in output or exit code for any command. Check 3 — "docs/index.md documents --shout" Run: `grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md` at the PR head and read the surrounding text. PASS: docs/index.md contains `--shout` and the text describes it as the flag that makes the greeting print in upper case. FAIL: `--shout` is absent from docs/index.md, or it is mentioned without saying what it does. Check 4 — "after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout" First determine whether the PR has been merged (`gh pr view --json state,mergedAt`). Then fetch the live page: `curl -sSL https://o.github.io/greet-cli/` and search the response for `--shout` (allow for HTML escaping, e.g. `–`/`–` or `--shout`). PASS: the PR is merged and the fetched published page contains `--shout`. FAIL: the fetched published page does not contain `--shout`, or the page cannot be fetched. If the PR is not yet merged, this check cannot pass: report it as FAIL with the reason "not merged yet, published page cannot be checked" and include what the live page currently shows. Do not pass this check from the contents of docs/index.md or the diff alone. Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL): - Also try `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout`; flag order independence is nice but not required by the lines above. - Confirm `npm test` passes and that new tests cover --shout and the unchanged default. - Note whether .github/workflows/pages.yml was left unchanged, since it is what publishes docs/ to the Pages site on push to main.

text:
I wrote both briefs for the `--shout` issue (#12) and the harness accepted them. One of the four acceptance lines can't pass until the PR is merged: the one that says the published docs page lists `--shout`.

**Builder brief:**
- Add a `--shout` flag in `bin/greet.js` that prints the whole greeting in upper case (e.g. `HELLO, ADA!`). It should work before or after the name.
- Leave the output without the flag exactly as it is now, including the usage message and exit code 2 when no name is given.
- Add tests to `test/greet.test.js` and make sure `npm test` passes.
- Document `--shout` in `docs/index.md`.
- Don't touch `.github/workflows/pages.yml` or try to publish anything. That workflow already deploys `docs/` to the docs site on every push to `main`, so merging the PR publishes the doc change.
- Say in the PR description that the published-docs line can only be confirmed after merge.

**Verifier brief:** one check per acceptance line, in order, each run at the PR head:
1. **Upper case:** run the program with `--shout` on two names and expect `HELLO, ADA!` and `HELLO, GRACE HOPPER!`.
2. **Unchanged without the flag:** compare stdout, stderr and exit code at the PR head against the base commit for two names and for the no-name case. Any difference fails.
3. **Docs file:** `docs/index.md` must contain `--shout` and say what it does.
4. **Published page:** check with `gh pr view` whether the PR is merged, then fetch https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ and look for `--shout`.
   - It passes only if the PR is merged and the live page shows the flag.
   - If the PR isn't merged, it's reported as FAIL with the reason "not merged yet, published page cannot be checked". It can't pass just because `docs/index.md` or the diff looks right.

Things the acceptance lines don't require are listed under "Advisory" and don't affect pass or fail: flag order, test coverage, and whether the workflow file was left unchanged.
